ai.description: This small 20–25 mm frog is brown with a distinct dark interorbital bar and a pale, inverted V-shaped mark on its back. It features granular skin and lacks webbing between its fingers.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Travancore Bush Frog is best identified by the distinct, pale-colored, hourglass-shaped marking on its back, which contrasts sharply with its darker body coloration.
ai.habitat: The Travancore Bush Frog inhabits the mid-to-high elevation evergreen forests of the southern Western Ghats, typically found at altitudes between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Travancore Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden within dense vegetation during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes travancoricus* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They lay small clutches of eggs in leaf axils, primarily during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Travancore Bush Frog is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically found at elevations between 900 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Travancore Bush Frog produces a high-pitched, insect-like "tink-tink" call consisting of rapid, repetitive pulses, typically heard from vegetation in humid forests.
